title: Chelsea Green Is Dealing With PTSD - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
1 hours ago
Chelsea Green is opening up about the frightening health battle that left her dealing with PTSD after waking up during heart surgery, revealing that the emotional aftermath of the procedure was even more difficult than she expected.
Speaking with TMZ’s “Inside the Ring” podcast, the WWE Superstar reflected on her long struggle with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), a heart condition that causes sudden episodes of an abnormally fast heartbeat. While Green says she’s now feeling better than ever and has returned to competing full-time, she admitted that the surgery to correct the condition left lasting emotional scars.
For years, Green struggled to get a definitive diagnosis because doctors were never able to capture one of her episodes while she was hooked up to an EKG. That finally changed during WrestleMania week while she was signing autographs at WWE World, allowing doctors to confirm the condition and move forward with treatment.

Before the surgery, Green said one of her biggest concerns was suffering an SVT episode during a WWE match in front of thousands of fans. She said,
“That was the fear. I cannot be in the ring in front of 10 or 20,000 people and go into tachycardia and still finish a match. The risk of death is obviously huge.”
“When I came out of it, I had like weird PTSD of being in that surgery and being woken up while still on the table and having them still operate.”
“For the last hour of the surgery or with some people maybe the last 20 minutes, they wake you up. They strap you down, they wake you up, you’ve got everything still going through your veins up into your heart, and they flush your IV with a medication that makes your heart speed up. So that exact feeling that I would get at the height of my SVT is what I felt immediately.”
“I did not know I had to wake up on the table and like go be operated on still. That’s very traumatizing.”
“The waking up in surgery traumatized me more than I thought it would and more than I had expected it to. And so that was just something like I needed to talk through and mentally get over that because there’s a lot of nightmares that I have about it. Now we’re a couple months out. I’ve spoken about it. I’m in the ring consistently every Friday night on Smackdown. I feel good. I feel better than I ever did before. I’m not getting the tachycardia attacks the way I used to. So it’s a relief.”
